asp_broken_dams.description: Gelt Rivermane's benches are a stair of beaver ponds, and the dams have held every spring without anybody's help since long before the camp arrived. This year three have gone inside a month. The quilboar have been cutting them, and they want the water gone, not the timber. A drained pond is dry ground to den in, and a dencarver would flood a whole valley before he spent another winter wet.
asp_broken_dams.accept_text: The dencarvers are down at the third pond on the Beaverdam Benches, a long way south of camp down the valley, and they've got good at it, and that bothers me. Bring the timber back up when you're done. The beavers will rebuild, they always do, but they rebuild faster with their own sticks.
asp_broken_dams.turn_in_text: They were back on it before you were out of the water. Did you see? Three years I've watched them put this valley together again every spring, with no plan and no elders and no argument about it. There's a lesson in that, and I'm too tired tonight to say what it is.

asp_cable_run.description: The main cable still comes off the drum and runs the thirty feet it always ran, and then it goes into the granite as though the granite had grown around it. Which, Nalu will point out in a very level voice, is approximately what happened. The rock didn't fall on the cable. The rock arrived where the cable already was.
asp_cable_run.accept_text: Follow it down to the face and look at where it enters. The harpies have been at the loose ends. They want the wire for their nests, and they've taken what they could reach. Bring me pieces and I can tell you how it parted. Mind the rim. It's a long way down, and there are only a few places to do it on purpose.
asp_cable_run.turn_in_text: Two of these are cut clean. The others are sheared, and wire only shears like that under load. So the cable was carrying when the ground came. Something was on it. I've spent three years not thinking that, and I'd like you to know you've ended a fairly useful habit.

asp_cornered_cold.description: The query from Tarren Mill asked whether there are yeti in Kalimdor. Mura Longstand's answer is that there are, that they're at the frozen end of a cave which is getting smaller every single year, and that she doesn't enjoy either half of that sentence. They came across inside the ice. Nobody carried them. They're refugees of the same accident that moved her people, and she's noticed, and it hasn't changed what has to be done.
asp_cornered_cold.turn_in_text: You went further in than I asked. You generally do. I'll write to the apothecary now. I'll tell him his impossible thing is real, that it's cornered, and that it's running out of cave. He'll be pleased. I've thought about it for a week, and I can't find the part I'm supposed to be pleased about.

asp_first_planks.description: Knowing which way the rot runs won't give you a floor. Longstand has a saw, a pile of bolts stacked the right way up at last, and not one person who's cut a board that came out true. Hateg would like the first honest stack this camp has produced, and he'd like somebody else's hands on the saw while he stands behind them and watches what they do wrong.
asp_first_planks.accept_text: I want boards I'd put in a wall, not attempts. The whole thing is the first cut. Get that off true and every board after that comes off true, and you won't find out until the wall is up and the door won't close. Take your time on the first one. The rest follow it whether you want them to or not.
asp_first_planks.turn_in_text: That's a stack of boards. That's an actual stack of actual boards. My father raised a tent frame every spring of his life and never once needed a plank for anything. I'm going to think about that later, when I'm less pleased with myself.

asp_green_wood.description: Hateg Barkhand has been told aspen is poor timber by three separate people who'd never put a hand on it. Green, it's heavy and soaking and splits like wet rope. Seasoned, it goes light as nothing and takes a nail without argument. The camp has been seasoning it wrong for two winters, because everything any of them knew about wood was about a different wood, on a different continent, under a different sky.
asp_green_wood.accept_text: I want standing dead, not fallen. Fallen has been lying in the wet, and it's no use to me whatever it looks like on the outside. Bolts will tell me whether the rot runs up from the root or down from the crown. Watch the lynx while you're cutting. They lie up in the deadfall, and you'll be bent over with an axe and your back to the slope.
asp_green_wood.turn_in_text: It runs down from the crown, every single one. So we've been stacking it upside down for two winters, in the rain, on purpose, for two whole winters. Don't tell Mura. I want to tell Mura.

asp_higher_every_spring.description: Hesta Coldshoulder has been measuring the creek on the benches for three years with a stick and a notch, and she's perfectly aware a stick and a notch won't pass for science. It's higher every spring. It's not by much, but it's by enough that she can't explain it with snowfall any more, and the water is coming out of a hole in the rim that wasn't a hole when she started counting.
asp_higher_every_spring.accept_text: The mouth is on the east side of the rim, above the old slide. You'll feel it before you see it, because the air coming out of that hole is wrong for this mountain. Go in as far as the shaft where the daylight comes down, and no further this trip. I want to know what the floor is. If it's wet rock, then I'm right about where my water is going.
asp_higher_every_spring.turn_in_text: So it's wet rock. Three years ago that was ice, and in three more it'll be a room. The range didn't arrive empty. It brought a glacier inside it, and the glacier is dying, and that's what has been running down into my ponds.

asp_red_ground.description: The camp downslope has lived under trees for three years and hasn't once stood on its own ground. Tomak has been quietly carrying Barrens soil down off the Seam, a sack at a time. It won't grow anything. It's for the floor of the elder's lodge, so that there's red dirt under somebody's feet when something important is being said over it.
asp_red_ground.accept_text: Take it off the dust side of the line, not the mould side. It has to be the real thing, or there's no point carrying it anywhere. The scavengers will be on you the whole time. They nest in the dead scrub, and they've worked out that a person crouching is a person not watching. Deal with them first, if you've got sense.
asp_red_ground.turn_in_text: It goes under the lodge floor tonight. Mura will stand on it and say nothing about it, and every single person in that camp will know what they're standing on, and that's how it should be done.

asp_rim_harpies.description: Garuk has been counting harpies since the thaw and doesn't care for the number. On the escarpment he can at least make sense of them. It's rock, it's a cliff, and a harpy belongs on a cliff. It's the ones further down that trouble him. There are harpies roosting in aspen crowns, in trees. Harpies don't do that, and something has taught them to.
asp_rim_harpies.accept_text: Work the rim first, then the stands beneath it. The tree-roosters are the dangerous ones. You don't see them until they're already dropping, and they've learned to wait, which is a word I don't enjoy using about harpies. I'm not asking for a cull. I'm asking for enough of a dent that I can tell Orgrimmar the number went down once.
asp_rim_harpies.turn_in_text: That'll do nicely. Write the tally in your own hand and I'll send it under mine. With two witnesses it's a report and not a rumour, and the Warchief has had three years of rumours about this mountain. He's had quite enough of them from people who came off that other world, as well, which I'm not saying to be unkind. I'm saying it because you'll be asked.

asp_rimehowl.description: At the far end of the Weeping Ice, past the braided passages and the standing meltwater, the glacier is still a glacier. The water drains down into it and doesn't come back out. That's where Rimehowl is, and he's there because it's the last ground left that's what he was made for. He won't leave it. There's nowhere to leave it to.
asp_rimehowl.accept_text: He's in the Sink. Follow the water down and it'll take you there, because that's the one thing water does reliably in that cave. He's bigger than the others and he isn't stupid. He'll give ground and let the cold do his work for him, so don't let a long fight become his fight. And take people with you. I'm not sending you in alone, and I wouldn't go in alone.
asp_rimehowl.turn_in_text: It's done, then. I'm not going to stand here and tell you I'm glad. He was the last of something, standing in the last of somewhere, and the only reason he was ever a danger to anybody is that his country melted out from under him. Ours went as well. We walked south, and he couldn't.

asp_rope_trade.description: Fizzik Quickline arrived on the rim with forty coils of rope and the unshakeable conviction that a cliff without a road down is the finest business proposition on the continent. He's right about that. He's also nearly out of rope, and harpy sinew is the only thing up here strong enough to replace it, which he says far too cheerfully.
asp_rope_trade.accept_text: Take the windcallers first. The plain ones mob you, but it's the callers that turn a mob into a problem, and I'd prefer you came back, because you're a repeat customer and those are precious. A full load of coils sees me through the season. I pay fair, which in my family is treated as a confession.
asp_rope_trade.turn_in_text: Fair is fair. And listen, the ways down are free. I'm not charging anybody for knowing where a gully is. Rope is a product. Knowing things is advertising. My cousins have never understood that.

asp_surveyors_pin.description: You turn it over. It's a surveyor's pin, brass, stamped with a number and a maker's mark you've never seen, and it was in a quilboar den, wrapped in hide, kept. The number is the part that stops you. Numbered pins come in a sequence, and a sequence means somebody walked this ground with a chain and a book and wrote down what they found, before any of this was here.
asp_surveyors_pin.accept_text: Hesta Coldshoulder keeps the watch up near the ice, and she has an eye for things that don't add up, which is most of this mountain. She'll know whether that mark is Horde, Alliance, or neither. The dencarvers will have more of them. They've been turning over this whole valley and keeping anything that shines.

asp_the_load.description: You turn the wire over in your hands. It's lift cable, the heavy grade, wound into the base of a harpy nest with the patience of something that simply liked the shape of it. The end hasn't been cut. It's been drawn out thin and snapped, the way wire goes when it's pulled past what it can hold. Something was hanging on this when the ground changed.
asp_the_load.accept_text: Nalu Stillgrass kept that winch eleven years. She'll know what a loaded cable end looks like, and she'll know what an empty one looks like, and she won't thank you for telling them apart. Take it to her. Look at the face under the Lift on the way, where the main line enters the rock, and see whether there's anything below it.
asp_the_load.turn_in_text: She doesn't say anything for a long moment. Then she says, "It was a full car, going down." She puts the wire in the iron chest with the ledgers, closes the lid, and sets her hand flat on top of it, and that's the end of the conversation for today.

asp_the_thaw.accept_text: Work the wet end, near the shaft. That's where the ice is going fastest, and that's where things are coming out of the wall. The bears denned in that cave when it was only a cave, and they aren't pleased about the company they've acquired. They're nearest the door for the same reason you'll be: it's the only warm part of the place. Mind you aren't between them and the way out.
asp_the_thaw.turn_in_text: There's a bone pin, a button, and something I'm not going to guess at in front of you. None of this is tauren work, and none of this is orcish. The ice picked these up somewhere else entirely and has just now put them down here. That's the second time this month I've had to write that sentence, and I didn't care for it the first time.

asp_uphill_boar.description: Owen Tallgrass watches Elkhorn because it's the only place in this zone where you can see anything at all. What he's been watching is quilboar coming up out of the Barrens in numbers, into a cold they've no clothing for and no word for. They were pushed. The mountain took their ground the same week it took the Lift. He points this out to people, and it's never once made anybody friendlier.
asp_uphill_boar.accept_text: The highrunners come up off the Slide, west of this meadow, and work its edges at first light. They're fast and they're desperate, and that's two problems arriving at once. Drop the frostspeakers first. Three years they've been trying to pray the cold back down, and whatever they're actually doing, it's what keeps the rest of them on their feet.
asp_uphill_boar.turn_in_text: That'll hold them off the meadow until the thaw. Then they'll come back, because they still have nowhere else to be, and we'll do all of this again. I'd like somebody cleverer than me to think about that part. I've been waiting three years for somebody to volunteer.

asp_ways_down.description: Ash Winterfall runs the chutes, which every elder in the camp has told him not to do. A chute is an avalanche path, swept bare every few winters by something enormous coming down it, and that scouring is exactly what makes it the only walkable line on a face of loose rock. The dangerous ground and the only road are the same ground. He finds this funnier than they do.
asp_ways_down.accept_text: Do three of the four. Take the middle one first, under the Lift. It's the widest, and if you can't manage that one you've no business on the others. Then the west gully and the east. Walk them, don't run them, and don't do it late on a warm afternoon when the sun has been sitting on the snowfield all day. That's when they go.
asp_ways_down.turn_in_text: That's the zone, then. Everything below the rim can be reached, and everything above is just the Barrens with a better view. Two winters I've been asking the elders for a proper trail crew. Perhaps they'll listen to somebody who's actually been down the thing.

asp_what_came_across.description: Mura Longstand has set two facts beside one another and doesn't care for the shape they make. A mountain arrived. Inside it was a glacier, and inside the glacier were animals that have no business on this continent and didn't walk here to get to it. The range didn't come empty. It came with its own country folded up inside it, and in three years nobody has asked how much of that country is still alive in there.
asp_what_came_across.accept_text: I've put the hide, the hair and the apothecary's own letter into one bundle with my mark burned into the wrap. Rimehowl's hide comes first, and he's at the bottom of the Weeping Ice, north-east of camp. Then take the bundle north, down off the mountain, to Tull at Camp Taurajo. Three years ago that man asked whether there was still a road south. The honest answer is that there's no road, there's a mountain, and the mountain has things living in it that aren't from here and never were. He'll want to be sitting down for the second part.
asp_what_came_across.turn_in_text: Tull reads it through twice, then lays his hand flat on the table on top of it. "So we were wrong to call it a wall," he says. "It's a country. Somebody else's country, dropped on top of ours, and we've spent three years treating it like weather." He doesn't say anything else for a long time, and he doesn't move his hand.

asp_winch_house.description: Keeper Nalu worked the north winch eleven years and was off shift the morning the ground changed. The house is still standing because the house was always on the Barrens side. The ledgers are still in it. So is a season of mail that was stacked and waiting to go down and never went. She's come back up most weeks since and hasn't once been able to open the box.
asp_winch_house.accept_text: The ledgers are in the iron chest under the drum. Bring me whatever the damp has left. The mail is loose in the sorting rack, and some of it will have blown into the scrub by now, so bring whatever is still readable. I know roughly what's in most of it. I'd still rather hold it than keep guessing.
asp_winch_house.turn_in_text: This one is a girl in Freewind writing to her brother on the top side. It's dated the week before. She's telling him about a horse. I'm not going to be able to deliver it and I'm going to keep it anyway, and I'd thank you not to have an opinion about that.

asp_winter_meat.description: Sani Quietstep hunted open plain her whole life, where you find a herd at dawn and you have it by noon, and the only question is how far you want to carry it. Up here the elk walk into timber and stop existing. She's got better at it. She isn't good at it yet, and the camp has to eat through a winter nobody has measured.
asp_winter_meat.accept_text: I need aspen elk. Work the edges of the stands, not the middle. They cross between cover in the same places every day, and up here that's the only predictable thing about them. Bring me good haunches and leave the thin ones. We aren't so short that we take a poor animal, and I'd rather not find out what we become once we start.
asp_winter_meat.turn_in_text: That's all of them, and not a thin one among them. You hunted the edges. I'll be good at this in another two winters. I'd rather have stayed bad at it on open ground, but nobody asked me and nobody is going to.

asp_wolf_nights.description: Mura Longstand will tell you the wolves aren't the problem, and she's right. They were here before the camp, and they've taken nothing but offal. The problem is that nobody in the camp sleeps, because the pack works the dark timber behind the sheds, and every person in Longstand grew up somewhere you could see a thing coming from a long way off.
asp_wolf_nights.accept_text: Thin the pack on Blackneedle Rise, east of camp, where the lodgepole starts. Don't take all of them. I won't have it said that we came into somebody else's country and emptied it. The bears are a separate matter. One has been at the smokehouse and has stopped being frightened of people, and at that point it stops being a bear and starts being a problem.
asp_wolf_nights.turn_in_text: The camp will sleep tonight. That's worth more than people who've always slept would guess at. And you left some, which is right. A place with nothing in the dark only feels safer. It's emptier, and I've seen what empty looks like.

asp_wrong_side.description: Watcher Tomak keeps the Seam, which in practice means watching things die slowly on the wrong side of it. The kodo are the worst. Barrens animals standing in snow, three years into a winter their kind has no word for, at a line they won't cross back over because there's nothing on the other side of it any more either.
asp_wrong_side.accept_text: I won't dress it up for you. They're suffering, they're going to keep suffering, and the only thing anyone can do for them is the thing nobody volunteers for. Do it clean and do it from the front, because they won't run, and it's worse if you make them try to.
asp_wrong_side.turn_in_text: My grandmother drove kodo. I grew up with one breathing against the tent flap all night. You did it properly, and from the front, and that counts for something. Most people do it from behind so they don't have to see the face.
